title: The emission rule: light separates from its source at $c - v$

statements.text: Relative to its source, light spreads in every direction at $c - v$ in absolute time, where $v$ is the source's speed in the absolute frame and $c$ the speed of light from a source at rest. The center of each light sphere moves along with the source.
statements.conditions: A source moving uniformly at $0 \le v < c$ in the absolute frame.

sources.quote: relative to its source, light spreads in every direction at c − v, measured using absolute time.
The forward-light assumption and the extension to all directions are the hypotheses behind this prediction, not consequences of absolute time alone.
